# Configuration reference

*Generated by `tools/gen_config_ref.py`. Do not edit this page: change the code or
`deploy/oss/.env.example`, then run `python tools/gen_config_ref.py`.*

Atlas is configured with `ATLAS_*` environment variables. In the OSS install they live in
`deploy/oss/.env` (copied from `deploy/oss/.env.example`), which compose reads for its own
`${...}` and passes to atlas-api and atlas-mcp. This page lists every variable the code
reads (98), grouped by area, and then the ones only the compose file reads.

How to read an entry:

- The description is the comment in `deploy/oss/.env.example`. Where several lines share
  one comment, the entry says which.
- **Allowed** comes from the constants in the code.
- **Default** is what the code uses when the variable is unset. It is shown only for a
  choice, a switch or a number; the code's text defaults suit the original install, not
  yours, so for a text setting use the OSS install's value.
- **OSS install** is the value `deploy/oss/.env.example` gives: set, or shown commented out
  as an example you can turn on.
- **Secret** says whether the value is a credential. A secret is never put in `.env`: set
  its `*_FILE` form to the path of a file holding it (`ATLAS_REQUIRE_SECRET_FILES=1`
  refuses the plain form).
- **Read by** is the process that reads it: atlas-api, atlas-mcp, or docker compose itself
  (and then what compose does with it), from the settings catalogue
  (`backend/settings_catalog.py`).

### `ATLAS_ACCEPTANCE_AGENT_WRITE`

Whether an agent may record acceptance on a workitem: off (default) \| attested.

- **Allowed:** `off`, `attested`
- **Default:** `off`
- **OSS install:** not set; `.env.example` shows `off` commented out
- **Secret:** no
- **Read by:** atlas-api

### `ATLAS_BEARER_HOSTS`

Derived from ATLAS_PUBLIC_URL while unset; set them only to widen or narrow that. *(This comment covers `ATLAS_LOGIN_ORIGINS` too.)*

- **Allowed:** comma-separated values
- **Default:** not shown for a text setting; see the OSS install's value
- **OSS install:** not set; `.env.example` shows `atlas.example.com,atlas.example.com:443` commented out
- **Secret:** no
- **Read by:** atlas-api

### `ATLAS_CONFIG_WRITES`

Configuration changes from the board: 1 lets an owner, in a browser session and with their password each time, change the few settings marked changeable on the Configuration tab (today ATLAS_STRICT_API and ATLAS_RETRIEVAL_TOP_K). A variable set in this file always wins over the board, so a setting assigned here cannot be changed there. 0, or unset, is read-only. An SSO-only owner has no password: with ATLAS_OIDC_STEP_UP=on they confirm each change with a fresh sign-in at the identity provider instead.

- **Allowed:** 1 or 0 (also true/false, yes/no, on/off)
- **Default:** `0`
- **OSS install:** not set; `.env.example` shows `0` commented out
- **Secret:** no
- **Read by:** atlas-api

### `ATLAS_INTERNAL_HOSTS`

Set by the compose file for this layout; listed so nobody sets them here by mistake: the API admits atlas-mcp's Bearer there only *(This comment covers `ATLAS_BASE_URL`, `ATLAS_CA_BUNDLE`, `ATLAS_TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS`, `ATLAS_CERT_EXPIRY_FILE` too.)*

- **Allowed:** comma-separated values
- **Default:** not shown for a text setting; see the OSS install's value
- **OSS install:** not set; `.env.example` shows `atlas-api:9443` commented out
- **Secret:** no
- **Read by:** atlas-api

### `ATLAS_LANDING`

Which public landing page "/" shows a visitor who is not signed in: v1 (today's short page) or v2 (the product website, first-party script under a strict Content-Security-Policy, ADR 0049). Unset = v1, and nothing else becomes public. v2 makes the website's own stylesheet, script and images readable without signing in, exact paths only.

- **Allowed:** `v1`, `v2`
- **Default:** `v1`
- **OSS install:** not set; `.env.example` shows `v2` commented out
- **Secret:** no
- **Read by:** atlas-api

### `ATLAS_LEGACY_V0`

The frozen v0 tables and /api/tree, /api/summary, /api/priority, /api/goals: off.

- **Allowed:** 1 or 0 (also true/false, yes/no, on/off)
- **Default:** `0`
- **OSS install:** `0`, set in `.env.example`
- **Secret:** no
- **Read by:** atlas-api

Derived from ATLAS_PUBLIC_URL while unset; set them only to widen or narrow that. *(This comment covers `ATLAS_BEARER_HOSTS` too.)*

The mailbox the privacy page names, and the product's display name. *(This comment covers `ATLAS_PRIVACY_CONTACT` too.)*

### `ATLAS_PUBLIC_DOCS`

The handbook at /docs (the documents of the atlas-system node, which none and demo both seed) readable without signing in: static pages only, the same text as the public repository (ADR 0047). 0, or unset, keeps /docs behind sign-in.

- **Allowed:** 1 or 0 (also true/false, yes/no, on/off)
- **Default:** `0`
- **OSS install:** `1`, set in `.env.example`
- **Secret:** no
- **Read by:** atlas-api

### `ATLAS_PUBLIC_URL`

The one absolute URL Atlas is reached on: https://ATLAS_PUBLIC_HOST, plus :ATLAS_TLS_PORT when that is not 443. The login origins and the hosts on which a Bearer token is honoured are derived from it. Keep it in step with the two values above.

- **Allowed:** an absolute URL
- **Default:** not shown for a text setting; see the OSS install's value
- **OSS install:** `https://atlas.example.com`, set in `.env.example`
- **Secret:** no
- **Read by:** atlas-api

### `ATLAS_SEED`

What an EMPTY database is seeded with: none (an empty instance), demo (one neutral example project) or self (Atlas's own world model: its parts, their documents and a reviewed set of intents, with no work items; regenerated by tools/export_self_seed.py). Read once, at the first start on an empty graph. The code default, homelab, is the personal tree.

- **Allowed:** `demo`, `none`, `self`
- **Default:** `none`
- **OSS install:** `none`, set in `.env.example`
- **Secret:** no
- **Read by:** atlas-api

### `ATLAS_SETUP_QUESTIONS_FILE`

The setup guide (an owner runs it through the atlas_setup_guide MCP tool) asks the shipped question set. To ask your own topics as well, name a JSON file of the same shape, mounted into atlas-api; its topics come after the shipped ones. Unset = the shipped set only.

- **Allowed:** a file path
- **Default:** not shown for a text setting; see the OSS install's value
- **OSS install:** not set; `.env.example` shows `/run/config/setup_questions.json` commented out
- **Secret:** no
- **Read by:** atlas-api

### `ATLAS_STRICT_API`

Strict API: a field POST/PATCH /api/node or /api/workitem would ignore (unknown, or not applied) is a 422 naming it, instead of a `warnings` entry on an accepted write (the default).

- **Allowed:** 1 or 0 (also true/false, yes/no, on/off)
- **Default:** `0`
- **OSS install:** `1`, set in `.env.example`
- **Secret:** no
- **Read by:** atlas-api

### `ATLAS_TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS`

Set by the compose file for this layout; listed so nobody sets them here by mistake: whose CF-Connecting-IP the API believes *(This comment covers `ATLAS_BASE_URL`, `ATLAS_CA_BUNDLE`, `ATLAS_INTERNAL_HOSTS`, `ATLAS_CERT_EXPIRY_FILE` too.)*

- **Allowed:** comma-separated values
- **Default:** not shown for a text setting; see the OSS install's value
- **OSS install:** not set; `.env.example` shows `<ATLAS_ORIGIN_SUBNET>` commented out
- **Secret:** no
- **Read by:** atlas-api

### `ATLAS_AUTH_PROVIDERS`

Providers: local \| oidc \| local,oidc. With oidc only, the login page shows "Sign in with SSO".

- **Allowed:** `local`, `oidc`
- **Default:** `local`
- **OSS install:** not set; `.env.example` shows `oidc` commented out
- **Secret:** no
- **Read by:** atlas-api

### `ATLAS_BREACH_CHECK`

The breached-password check against the bundled list, with no outbound call (the API has no route out in this layout).

- **Allowed:** `remote`, `bundled`
- **Default:** `remote`
- **OSS install:** `bundled`, set in `.env.example`
- **Secret:** no
- **Read by:** atlas-api

### `ATLAS_LOCAL_LOGIN`

Password login: all (every local account) \| break-glass (only accounts made with `atlas-admin user add &lt;name&gt; --role owner --break-glass`, at the unlinked /auth/login?break_glass=1; every use is a `login_break_glass` auth_event). Keep the break-glass credential in the enterprise vault: it is how you get in when the IdP is down.

- **Allowed:** `all`, `break-glass`
- **Default:** `all`
- **OSS install:** not set; `.env.example` shows `break-glass` commented out
- **Secret:** no
- **Read by:** atlas-api

### `ATLAS_MCP_OAUTH_SCOPES`

The scopes a client should request, verbatim as the IdP names them (sent in the metadata and the 401 challenge). Entra: the full api://&lt;app&gt;/&lt;scope&gt; form.

- **Allowed:** comma-separated values
- **Default:** not shown for a text setting; see the OSS install's value
- **OSS install:** not set; `.env.example` shows `api://<resource app id>/Atlas.Write` commented out
- **Secret:** no
- **Read by:** atlas-mcp

### `ATLAS_OAUTH_AUDIENCES`

Further accepted audiences. Entra v2 access tokens carry the resource app's client id (the app registration that exposes the API, never ATLAS_OIDC_CLIENT_ID), not the URI:

- **Allowed:** comma-separated values
- **Default:** not shown for a text setting; see the OSS install's value
- **OSS install:** not set; `.env.example` shows `<resource app (client) id>` commented out
- **Secret:** no
- **Read by:** atlas-api

### `ATLAS_OAUTH_RESOURCE`

The resource: the MCP endpoint as clients reach it. The token's `aud` must carry it. That is the main door's /mcp, as written in the client's URL: add :ATLAS_TLS_PORT only when the port is not 443 (it is compared as written, so :443 here and none in the client's URL differ).

- **Allowed:** an absolute URL
- **Default:** not shown for a text setting; see the OSS install's value
- **OSS install:** not set; `.env.example` shows `https://atlas.example.com/mcp` commented out
- **Secret:** no
- **Read by:** atlas-api, atlas-mcp

### `ATLAS_OAUTH_SCOPE_MAP`

IdP scope -&gt; Atlas tier (read \| write \| admin); the highest wins, nothing mapped is read-only, and the person's role and project roles still cap it.

- **Allowed:** IdP scope=tier pairs; tiers: read, write, admin
- **Default:** not shown for a text setting; see the OSS install's value
- **OSS install:** not set; `.env.example` shows `Atlas.Read=read,Atlas.Write=write` commented out
- **Secret:** no
- **Read by:** atlas-api

### `ATLAS_OIDC_CLIENT_ID`

The issuer (discovery is read from &lt;issuer&gt;/.well-known/openid-configuration) and the client. Entra ID: https://login.microsoftonline.com/&lt;tenant-id&gt;/v2.0 with ATLAS_OIDC_PRESET=entra (a tenant id, never common/organizations). Keycloak: https://&lt;host&gt;/realms/&lt;realm&gt; with ATLAS_OIDC_PRESET=keycloak. *(This comment covers `ATLAS_OIDC_ISSUER`, `ATLAS_OIDC_PRESET` too.)*

- **Allowed:** text
- **Default:** not shown for a text setting; see the OSS install's value
- **OSS install:** not set; `.env.example` shows `<application (client) id>` commented out
- **Secret:** no
- **Read by:** atlas-api

### `ATLAS_OIDC_CLIENT_KEY`

Or a key instead of a secret (Entra: a certificate credential; KEY_ID is its base64url SHA-1 thumbprint, sent as x5t). oidc.yml mounts it at /run/secrets/oidc_client_key once ATLAS_OIDC_CLIENT_KEY_SOURCE below names the file: *(This comment covers `ATLAS_OIDC_TOKEN_AUTH`, `ATLAS_OIDC_CLIENT_KEY_FILE`, `ATLAS_OIDC_CLIENT_KEY_ID` too.)*

- **Allowed:** a secret, given as the path of a file holding it
- **Default:** not shown for a text setting; see the OSS install's value
- **OSS install:** not set; `.env.example` shows `/run/secrets/oidc_client_key` (as `ATLAS_OIDC_CLIENT_KEY_FILE`) commented out
- **Secret:** yes: set `ATLAS_OIDC_CLIENT_KEY_FILE` to the path of a file; the plain variable is never read
- **Read by:** atlas-api

### `ATLAS_OIDC_CLIENT_KEY_ID`

Or a key instead of a secret (Entra: a certificate credential; KEY_ID is its base64url SHA-1 thumbprint, sent as x5t). oidc.yml mounts it at /run/secrets/oidc_client_key once ATLAS_OIDC_CLIENT_KEY_SOURCE below names the file: *(This comment covers `ATLAS_OIDC_TOKEN_AUTH`, `ATLAS_OIDC_CLIENT_KEY_FILE` too.)*

- **Allowed:** text
- **Default:** not shown for a text setting
- **OSS install:** not set
- **Secret:** no
- **Read by:** atlas-api

### `ATLAS_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET`

How Atlas authenticates at the token endpoint (client_secret_basic, client_secret_post or private_key_jwt), and the client credential, which is a FILE (the plain variable is refused). The overlay oidc.yml (docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f oidc.yml) mounts ./secrets/oidc_client_secret at /run/secrets/oidc_client_secret, and gives atlas-api its route to the IdP (`egress`). *(This comment covers `ATLAS_OIDC_TOKEN_AUTH`, `ATLAS_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET_FILE` too.)*

- **Allowed:** a secret, given as the path of a file holding it
- **Default:** not shown for a text setting; see the OSS install's value
- **OSS install:** not set; `.env.example` shows `/run/secrets/oidc_client_secret` (as `ATLAS_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET_FILE`) commented out
- **Secret:** yes: set `ATLAS_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET_FILE` to the path of a file; the plain variable is never read
- **Read by:** atlas-api

A preset's claim names, overridden one at a time (e.g. groups from `roles`). *(This comment covers `ATLAS_OIDC_NAME_CLAIM`, `ATLAS_OIDC_GROUPS_CLAIM` too.)*

- **Allowed:** text

A preset's claim names, overridden one at a time (e.g. groups from `roles`). *(This comment covers `ATLAS_OIDC_NAME_CLAIM`, `ATLAS_OIDC_EMAIL_CLAIM` too.)*

- **Allowed:** text
- **Default:** not shown for a text setting

### `ATLAS_OIDC_GROUP_MAP_FILE`

Groups. Only the IdP groups listed in the map file reach Atlas (a YAML `groups:` mapping of IdP group value -&gt; Atlas group name; Entra: the group's object id, Keycloak: its path), and a user's IdP memberships are replaced from the token at every login. Entra omits the groups claim past ~200 groups ("overage") and Atlas then REFUSES the login: configure the app registration to emit only "Groups assigned to the application".

- **Allowed:** a file path
- **Default:** not shown for a text setting; see the OSS install's value
- **OSS install:** not set; `.env.example` shows `/run/secrets/oidc_group_map` commented out
- **Secret:** no
- **Read by:** atlas-api

### `ATLAS_OIDC_ISSUER`

The issuer (discovery is read from &lt;issuer&gt;/.well-known/openid-configuration) and the client. Entra ID: https://login.microsoftonline.com/&lt;tenant-id&gt;/v2.0 with ATLAS_OIDC_PRESET=entra (a tenant id, never common/organizations). Keycloak: https://&lt;host&gt;/realms/&lt;realm&gt; with ATLAS_OIDC_PRESET=keycloak. *(This comment covers `ATLAS_OIDC_PRESET`, `ATLAS_OIDC_CLIENT_ID` too.)*

- **Allowed:** an absolute URL
- **Default:** not shown for a text setting; see the OSS install's value
- **OSS install:** not set; `.env.example` shows `https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant-id>/v2.0` commented out
- **Secret:** no
- **Read by:** atlas-api, atlas-mcp

### `ATLAS_OIDC_MAX_SESSION_HOURS`

Offboarding: an SSO session lasts at most this long, and a person's agent tokens stop working this many days after their last SSO login (until they sign in again). *(This comment covers `ATLAS_OIDC_REVALIDATE_DAYS` too.)*

- **Allowed:** 1 to 336
- **Default:** `12`
- **OSS install:** not set; `.env.example` shows `12` commented out
- **Secret:** no
- **Read by:** atlas-api

### `ATLAS_OIDC_NAME_CLAIM`

A preset's claim names, overridden one at a time (e.g. groups from `roles`). *(This comment covers `ATLAS_OIDC_EMAIL_CLAIM`, `ATLAS_OIDC_GROUPS_CLAIM` too.)*

- **Allowed:** text
- **Default:** not shown for a text setting
- **OSS install:** not set
- **Secret:** no
- **Read by:** atlas-api

### `ATLAS_OIDC_PRESET`

The issuer (discovery is read from &lt;issuer&gt;/.well-known/openid-configuration) and the client. Entra ID: https://login.microsoftonline.com/&lt;tenant-id&gt;/v2.0 with ATLAS_OIDC_PRESET=entra (a tenant id, never common/organizations). Keycloak: https://&lt;host&gt;/realms/&lt;realm&gt; with ATLAS_OIDC_PRESET=keycloak. *(This comment covers `ATLAS_OIDC_ISSUER`, `ATLAS_OIDC_CLIENT_ID` too.)*

- **Allowed:** `generic`, `entra`, `keycloak`
- **Default:** `generic`
- **OSS install:** not set; `.env.example` shows `entra` commented out
- **Secret:** no
- **Read by:** atlas-api

### `ATLAS_OIDC_REDIRECT_URI`

The callback URL sent to the IdP; it must equal the redirect URI registered there. Derived from ATLAS_PUBLIC_URL while unset.

- **Allowed:** an absolute URL
- **Default:** not shown for a text setting; see the OSS install's value
- **OSS install:** not set; `.env.example` shows `https://atlas.example.com/auth/oidc/callback` commented out
- **Secret:** no
- **Read by:** atlas-api

### `ATLAS_OIDC_REQUIRED_GROUPS`

Accounts are created at first login (as member) only for someone in one of these IdP groups, and every login needs one. Unset = no automatic accounts at all.

- **Allowed:** comma-separated values
- **Default:** not shown for a text setting; see the OSS install's value
- **OSS install:** not set; `.env.example` shows `<atlas-users group object id>` commented out
- **Secret:** no
- **Read by:** atlas-api

### `ATLAS_OIDC_REVALIDATE_DAYS`

Offboarding: an SSO session lasts at most this long, and a person's agent tokens stop working this many days after their last SSO login (until they sign in again). *(This comment covers `ATLAS_OIDC_MAX_SESSION_HOURS` too.)*

- **Allowed:** 1 to 3650
- **Default:** `30`
- **OSS install:** not set; `.env.example` shows `30` commented out
- **Secret:** no
- **Read by:** atlas-api

### `ATLAS_OIDC_SCOPES`

The scopes requested at the authorization endpoint, space-separated; openid is required, and a list without it stops atlas-api at boot.

- **Allowed:** text
- **Default:** not shown for a text setting; see the OSS install's value
- **OSS install:** not set; `.env.example` shows `openid profile email` commented out
- **Secret:** no
- **Read by:** atlas-api

### `ATLAS_OIDC_STEP_UP`

Agent credentials for SSO people (TASK-1415). Creating one under Settings, Agent credentials, asks for the person's password again, and an SSO account has none. With step-up on, an SSO person confirms with a FRESH sign-in at the IdP instead (prompt=login, max_age), and the credential is created only if the ID token's auth_time is at most MAX_AGE seconds old. Local accounts (break-glass) keep the password prompt. Off: today, password for everyone. Entra ID: add the optional claim auth_time to the ID token in the app registration. *(This comment covers `ATLAS_OIDC_STEP_UP_MAX_AGE_SECONDS` too.)*

- **Allowed:** `off`, `on`
- **Default:** `off`
- **OSS install:** not set; `.env.example` shows `on` commented out
- **Secret:** no
- **Read by:** atlas-api

### `ATLAS_OIDC_STEP_UP_MAX_AGE_SECONDS`

Agent credentials for SSO people (TASK-1415). Creating one under Settings, Agent credentials, asks for the person's password again, and an SSO account has none. With step-up on, an SSO person confirms with a FRESH sign-in at the IdP instead (prompt=login, max_age), and the credential is created only if the ID token's auth_time is at most MAX_AGE seconds old. Local accounts (break-glass) keep the password prompt. Off: today, password for everyone. Entra ID: add the optional claim auth_time to the ID token in the app registration. *(This comment covers `ATLAS_OIDC_STEP_UP` too.)*

- **Allowed:** 60 to 900
- **Default:** `300`
- **OSS install:** not set; `.env.example` shows `300` commented out
- **Secret:** no
- **Read by:** atlas-api

### `ATLAS_OIDC_TOKEN_AUTH`

How Atlas authenticates at the token endpoint (client_secret_basic, client_secret_post or private_key_jwt), and the client credential, which is a FILE (the plain variable is refused). The overlay oidc.yml (docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f oidc.yml) mounts ./secrets/oidc_client_secret at /run/secrets/oidc_client_secret, and gives atlas-api its route to the IdP (`egress`).
Or a key instead of a secret (Entra: a certificate credential; KEY_ID is its base64url SHA-1 thumbprint, sent as x5t). oidc.yml mounts it at /run/secrets/oidc_client_key once ATLAS_OIDC_CLIENT_KEY_SOURCE below names the file: *(This comment covers `ATLAS_OIDC_CLIENT_KEY_FILE`, `ATLAS_OIDC_CLIENT_KEY_ID` too.)*

- **Allowed:** `client_secret_basic`, `client_secret_post`, `private_key_jwt`
- **Default:** `client_secret_basic`
- **OSS install:** not set; `.env.example` shows `client_secret_basic`, `private_key_jwt` commented out
- **Secret:** no
- **Read by:** atlas-api

- **Default:** `1`
- **OSS install:** `false`, set in `.env.example`
- **Secret:** no
- **Read by:** atlas-api

### `ATLAS_RBAC`

Project-scoped RBAC: roles on projects, private by default, shared projects read-only for everyone else, and an instance admin is not an implicit owner of every project. *(This comment covers `ATLAS_DEFAULT_PROJECT_VISIBILITY`, `ATLAS_SHARED_PROJECT_ROLE`, `ATLAS_INSTANCE_ADMIN_IMPLICIT_PROJECT_OWNER` too.)*

Project-scoped RBAC: roles on projects, private by default, shared projects read-only for everyone else, and an instance admin is not an implicit owner of every project. *(This comment covers `ATLAS_RBAC`, `ATLAS_DEFAULT_PROJECT_VISIBILITY`, `ATLAS_INSTANCE_ADMIN_IMPLICIT_PROJECT_OWNER` too.)*

- **Default:** `editor`

## TLS and the internal hop

| Variable | Code default | OSS .env.example | Secret | Read by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [`ATLAS_BASE_URL`](#atlas_base_url) | - | commented out | no | atlas-mcp |
| [`ATLAS_CA_BUNDLE`](#atlas_ca_bundle) | - | commented out | no | atlas-mcp |
| [`ATLAS_CERT_EXPIRY_FILE`](#atlas_cert_expiry_file) | - | commented out | no | atlas-api |
| [`ATLAS_CERT_EXPIRY_WARN_DAYS`](#atlas_cert_expiry_warn_days) | `30` | commented out | no | atlas-api |
| [`ATLAS_MCP_CLIENT_CERT_FILE`](#atlas_mcp_client_cert_file) | - | commented out | no | atlas-mcp |
| [`ATLAS_MCP_CLIENT_KEY_FILE`](#atlas_mcp_client_key_file) | - | commented out | yes | atlas-mcp |

### `ATLAS_BASE_URL`

Set by the compose file for this layout; listed so nobody sets them here by mistake: where atlas-mcp reaches the API *(This comment covers `ATLAS_CA_BUNDLE`, `ATLAS_INTERNAL_HOSTS`, `ATLAS_TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS`, `ATLAS_CERT_EXPIRY_FILE` too.)*

- **Allowed:** an absolute URL
- **Default:** not shown for a text setting; see the OSS install's value
- **OSS install:** not set; `.env.example` shows `https://atlas-api:9443` commented out
- **Secret:** no
- **Read by:** atlas-mcp

### `ATLAS_CA_BUNDLE`

Set by the compose file for this layout; listed so nobody sets them here by mistake: the CA atlas-mcp trusts (= ./secrets/tls/ca.crt) *(This comment covers `ATLAS_BASE_URL`, `ATLAS_INTERNAL_HOSTS`, `ATLAS_TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS`, `ATLAS_CERT_EXPIRY_FILE` too.)*

- **Allowed:** a file path
- **Default:** not shown for a text setting; see the OSS install's value
- **OSS install:** not set; `.env.example` shows `/run/secrets/atlas_ca` commented out
- **Secret:** no
- **Read by:** atlas-mcp

### `ATLAS_CERT_EXPIRY_FILE`

Set by the compose file for this layout; listed so nobody sets them here by mistake: the certificate /api/health watches (= ./secrets/tls/server.crt) *(This comment covers `ATLAS_BASE_URL`, `ATLAS_CA_BUNDLE`, `ATLAS_INTERNAL_HOSTS`, `ATLAS_TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS` too.)*

- **Allowed:** a file path
- **Default:** not shown for a text setting; see the OSS install's value
- **OSS install:** not set; `.env.example` shows `/run/secrets/tls_cert` commented out
- **Secret:** no
- **Read by:** atlas-api

### `ATLAS_CERT_EXPIRY_WARN_DAYS`

Certificate expiry (TASK-1419). /api/health lists the server certificate under `cert_warnings` once it is this many days from expiry (1-3650, default 30), and when it has expired. init-certs.sh issues it for 397 days; renew with `init-certs.sh --force` (docs/oss/guides/operations.md, section 5, "The expiry warning").

- **Allowed:** 1 to 3650 days
- **Default:** `30`
- **OSS install:** not set; `.env.example` shows `30` commented out
- **Secret:** no
- **Read by:** atlas-api

### `ATLAS_MCP_CLIENT_CERT_FILE`

The mTLS leg on atlas-mcp's hop to the API: off (default) \| require. With require, atlas-tls refuses a connection to atlas-api:9443 without a client certificate issued by the CA in ATLAS_TLS_CLIENT_CA_FILE (default ./secrets/tls/client-ca.crt), and atlas-mcp presents its own: uncomment the two ATLAS_MCP_CLIENT_* lines together with this one. *(This comment covers `ATLAS_TLS_CLIENT_AUTH`, `ATLAS_TLS_CLIENT_CA_FILE`, `ATLAS_MCP_CLIENT_KEY_FILE` too.)*

- **Allowed:** a file path
- **Default:** not shown for a text setting; see the OSS install's value
- **OSS install:** not set; `.env.example` shows `/run/secrets/mcp_client_cert` commented out
- **Secret:** no
- **Read by:** atlas-mcp

### `ATLAS_MCP_CLIENT_KEY_FILE`

The mTLS leg on atlas-mcp's hop to the API: off (default) \| require. With require, atlas-tls refuses a connection to atlas-api:9443 without a client certificate issued by the CA in ATLAS_TLS_CLIENT_CA_FILE (default ./secrets/tls/client-ca.crt), and atlas-mcp presents its own: uncomment the two ATLAS_MCP_CLIENT_* lines together with this one. *(This comment covers `ATLAS_TLS_CLIENT_AUTH`, `ATLAS_TLS_CLIENT_CA_FILE`, `ATLAS_MCP_CLIENT_CERT_FILE` too.)*

- **Allowed:** a file path
- **Default:** not shown for a text setting; see the OSS install's value
- **OSS install:** not set; `.env.example` shows `/run/secrets/mcp_client_key` commented out
- **Secret:** yes: this is the path of a file holding a credential
- **Read by:** atlas-mcp

| [`ATLAS_EMBED_DIM`](#atlas_embed_dim) | - | commented out | no | atlas-api |
| [`ATLAS_EMBED_DOC_PREFIX`](#atlas_embed_doc_prefix) | - | - | no | atlas-api |
| [`ATLAS_EMBED_ENTRA_SCOPE`](#atlas_embed_entra_scope) | - | commented out | no | atlas-api |
| [`ATLAS_EMBED_KEY`](#atlas_embed_key) | - | commented out | yes | atlas-api |
| [`ATLAS_EMBED_KEY_FILE`](#atlas_embed_key_file) | - | commented out | yes | atlas-api |
| [`ATLAS_EMBED_MODEL`](#atlas_embed_model) | - | commented out | no | atlas-api |
| [`ATLAS_EMBED_QUERY_PREFIX`](#atlas_embed_query_prefix) | - | - | no | atlas-api |
| [`ATLAS_EMBED_SCOPE`](#atlas_embed_scope) | `shared` | commented out | no | atlas-api |
| [`ATLAS_EMBED_URL`](#atlas_embed_url) | - | commented out | no | atlas-api |

| [`ATLAS_RETRIEVAL_TOP_K`](#atlas_retrieval_top_k) | `30` | commented out | no | atlas-api |

### `ATLAS_EMBED_AUTH_HEADER`

bearer (Authorization: Bearer with the key), api-key (Azure OpenAI's header), or entra: an Entra ID token from the workload identity (AZURE_FEDERATED_TOKEN_FILE, AZURE_CLIENT_ID, AZURE_TENANT_ID; the overlay retrieval-workload-identity.yml mounts the token) or managed identity the container runs as. entra takes no key file.

- **Allowed:** `bearer`, `api-key`, `entra`
- **Default:** `bearer`
- **OSS install:** not set; `.env.example` shows `bearer` commented out
- **Secret:** no
- **Read by:** atlas-api

### `ATLAS_EMBED_BATCH`

Texts per embeddings call, and seconds between index passes. *(This comment covers `ATLAS_RETRIEVAL_INTERVAL_S` too.)*

- **Allowed:** a whole number
- **Default:** `32`
- **OSS install:** not set; `.env.example` shows `32` commented out
- **Secret:** no
- **Read by:** atlas-api

### `ATLAS_EMBED_CA_BUNDLE`

A PEM bundle for an endpoint whose certificate is from a private CA (e.g. /run/secrets/atlas_ca).

- **Allowed:** a file path
- **Default:** not shown for a text setting
- **OSS install:** not set
- **Secret:** no
- **Read by:** atlas-api

### `ATLAS_EMBED_DIM`

The vector length the endpoint returns for that model, and the size of the vector column (at most 16000). A vector of another length is refused; changing it on an index that holds vectors needs POST /api/retrieval/reindex with rebuild=true.

- **Allowed:** a positive whole number
- **Default:** none (unset)
- **OSS install:** not set; `.env.example` shows `1536` commented out
- **Secret:** no
- **Read by:** atlas-api

### `ATLAS_EMBED_DOC_PREFIX`

Text put verbatim before every indexed chunk, for a model trained with one (nomic-embed-text: "search_document: ", trailing space included). Empty by default; changing it re-embeds.

- **Allowed:** text
- **Default:** not shown for a text setting
- **OSS install:** not set
- **Secret:** no
- **Read by:** atlas-api

### `ATLAS_EMBED_ENTRA_SCOPE`

The token scope in entra mode (a sovereign cloud has its own).

- **Allowed:** text
- **Default:** not shown for a text setting; see the OSS install's value
- **OSS install:** not set; `.env.example` shows `https://cognitiveservices.azure.com/.default` commented out
- **Secret:** no
- **Read by:** atlas-api

### `ATLAS_EMBED_KEY`

The PATH of the file holding the endpoint's key, read on every call (a rotated key needs no restart); unset for an endpoint that takes no key, and in entra mode. retrieval.yml mounts ./secrets/embed_key there. The key is only ever a file: a plain ATLAS_EMBED_KEY variable makes the add-on unavailable.

- **Allowed:** a secret, given as the path of a file holding it
- **Default:** not shown for a text setting; see the OSS install's value
- **OSS install:** not set; `.env.example` shows `/run/secrets/embed_key` (as `ATLAS_EMBED_KEY_FILE`) commented out
- **Secret:** yes: set `ATLAS_EMBED_KEY_FILE` to the path of a file; the plain variable is never read
- **Read by:** atlas-api

### `ATLAS_EMBED_KEY_FILE`

The PATH of the file holding the endpoint's key, read on every call (a rotated key needs no restart); unset for an endpoint that takes no key, and in entra mode. retrieval.yml mounts ./secrets/embed_key there. The key is only ever a file: a plain ATLAS_EMBED_KEY variable makes the add-on unavailable.

- **Allowed:** a file path
- **Default:** not shown for a text setting; see the OSS install's value
- **OSS install:** not set; `.env.example` shows `/run/secrets/embed_key` commented out
- **Secret:** yes: this is the path of a file holding a credential
- **Read by:** atlas-api

### `ATLAS_EMBED_MODEL`

The model name, sent as `model` on every call and stored on every indexed row; changing it re-embeds everything (vectors of two models are never mixed).

- **Allowed:** text
- **Default:** not shown for a text setting; see the OSS install's value
- **OSS install:** not set; `.env.example` shows `text-embedding-3-small` commented out
- **Secret:** no
- **Read by:** atlas-api

### `ATLAS_EMBED_QUERY_PREFIX`

Text put verbatim before every search query, the query side of the same convention (nomic: "search_query: "). Empty by default.

- **Allowed:** text
- **Default:** not shown for a text setting
- **OSS install:** not set
- **Secret:** no
- **Read by:** atlas-api

### `ATLAS_EMBED_SCOPE`

shared never sends the text of a private project to the endpoint; all sends everything.

- **Allowed:** `shared`, `all`
- **Default:** `shared`
- **OSS install:** not set; `.env.example` shows `shared` commented out
- **Secret:** no
- **Read by:** atlas-api

### `ATLAS_EMBED_URL`

https:// is required (plain http only to loopback). A `/v1` base gets `/embeddings` appended; a URL ending in /embeddings is used as given, query string included.

- **Allowed:** an absolute URL
- **Default:** not shown for a text setting; see the OSS install's value
- **OSS install:** not set; `.env.example` shows `https://<your-endpoint>/openai/deployments/<deployment>/embeddings?api-version=2024-10-21` commented out
- **Secret:** no
- **Read by:** atlas-api

### `ATLAS_RETRIEVAL`

The base install has keyword search only. To turn the add-on on, set the block below and start with the overlay: `docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f retrieval.yml up -d` (it gives atlas-api its route out and the key as the secret ./secrets/embed_key). It runs inside atlas-api and reaches embeddings only through this OpenAI-compatible endpoint; no model ships in any image. A broken configuration never stops Atlas: /api/health says `retrieval: unavailable: &lt;reason&gt;`, and search stays full-text.

- **Allowed:** `off`, `on`
- **Default:** `off`
- **OSS install:** not set; `.env.example` shows `off` commented out
- **Secret:** no
- **Read by:** atlas-api

### `ATLAS_RETRIEVAL_INTERVAL_S`

Texts per embeddings call, and seconds between index passes. *(This comment covers `ATLAS_EMBED_BATCH` too.)*

- **Allowed:** a whole number
- **Default:** `60`
- **OSS install:** not set; `.env.example` shows `60` commented out
- **Secret:** no
- **Read by:** atlas-api

### `ATLAS_RETRIEVAL_TOP_K`

How many nodes the vector list contributes to a mode=semantic\|hybrid search (1-200).

- **Allowed:** 1 to 200
- **Default:** `30`
- **OSS install:** not set; `.env.example` shows `30` commented out
- **Secret:** no
- **Read by:** atlas-api

## atlas-mcp

| Variable | Code default | OSS .env.example | Secret | Read by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [`ATLAS_MCP_ALLOWED_HOSTS`](#atlas_mcp_allowed_hosts) | - | set | no | atlas-mcp |
| [`ATLAS_MCP_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`](#atlas_mcp_allowed_origins) | - | set | no | atlas-mcp |
| [`ATLAS_MCP_ALLOW_SHARED_TOKEN`](#atlas_mcp_allow_shared_token) | `0` | - | no | atlas-mcp |
| [`ATLAS_MCP_AUTH_CACHE_S`](#atlas_mcp_auth_cache_s) | `60` | commented out | no | atlas-mcp |
| [`ATLAS_MCP_ENABLE_DELETE`](#atlas_mcp_enable_delete) | `0` | commented out | no | atlas-mcp |
| [`ATLAS_MCP_STATELESS_HTTP`](#atlas_mcp_stateless_http) | `0` | commented out | no | atlas-mcp |
| [`ATLAS_TOKEN`](#atlas_token) | - | - | yes | atlas-mcp |

### `ATLAS_MCP_ALLOWED_HOSTS`

The Host headers atlas-mcp answers on /mcp (DNS-rebinding protection; any other Host is a 421). Clients arrive through atlas-tls with the public name; loopback serves the container's own health probe. Add ATLAS_PUBLIC_HOST:ATLAS_TLS_PORT when the port is not 443. atlas-mcp:9444 is the gateway profile's hop (atlas-tls sets that Host on it); harmless without the profile, required with it.

- **Allowed:** comma-separated values
- **Default:** not shown for a text setting; see the OSS install's value
- **OSS install:** `atlas.example.com,atlas.example.com:443,localhost:*,127.0.0.1:*,atlas-mcp:9444`, set in `.env.example`
- **Secret:** no
- **Read by:** atlas-mcp

### `ATLAS_MCP_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`

Checked only when a request sends an Origin header (browsers do; MCP clients do not).

- **Allowed:** comma-separated values
- **Default:** not shown for a text setting; see the OSS install's value
- **OSS install:** `https://atlas.example.com`, set in `.env.example`
- **Secret:** no
- **Read by:** atlas-mcp

### `ATLAS_MCP_ALLOW_SHARED_TOKEN`

The shared-token migration fallback is for the homelab's history only. Leave both unset: every caller sends its own Bearer token. (ATLAS_TOKEN would be a secret: ATLAS_TOKEN_FILE.) *(This comment covers `ATLAS_TOKEN_FILE` too.)*

- **Allowed:** on for 1/true/yes/on; anything else is off
- **Default:** `0`
- **OSS install:** not set
- **Secret:** no
- **Read by:** atlas-mcp

### `ATLAS_MCP_AUTH_CACHE_S`

How long the door remembers that the API accepted a token, in seconds.

- **Allowed:** seconds
- **Default:** `60`
- **OSS install:** not set; `.env.example` shows `60` commented out
- **Secret:** no
- **Read by:** atlas-mcp

### `ATLAS_MCP_ENABLE_DELETE`

Offer atlas_delete. Grants nothing: each call still needs the caller's own admin scope.

- **Allowed:** on for 1/true/yes/on; anything else is off
- **Default:** `0`
- **OSS install:** not set; `.env.example` shows `1` commented out
- **Secret:** no
- **Read by:** atlas-mcp

### `ATLAS_MCP_STATELESS_HTTP`

Run more than one atlas-mcp replica behind a load balancer: 1 switches the MCP transport to stateless Streamable HTTP, so no session is kept in memory and any replica answers any request. Auth is unchanged: every request still carries the caller's own token. Unset or 0 keeps the stateful sessions, which is all a single replica needs.

- **Allowed:** 1 or 0 (also true/false, yes/no, on/off)
- **Default:** `0`
- **OSS install:** not set; `.env.example` shows `1` commented out
- **Secret:** no
- **Read by:** atlas-mcp

### `ATLAS_TOKEN`

The shared-token migration fallback is for the homelab's history only. Leave both unset: every caller sends its own Bearer token. (ATLAS_TOKEN would be a secret: ATLAS_TOKEN_FILE.) *(This comment covers `ATLAS_MCP_ALLOW_SHARED_TOKEN`, `ATLAS_TOKEN_FILE` too.)*

- **Allowed:** a secret, given as the path of a file holding it
- **Default:** not shown for a text setting
- **OSS install:** not set
- **Secret:** yes: set `ATLAS_TOKEN_FILE` to the path of a file; the plain variable is refused when `ATLAS_REQUIRE_SECRET_FILES` is on
- **Read by:** atlas-mcp

## Read audit

| Variable | Code default | OSS .env.example | Secret | Read by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [`ATLAS_AUDIT_READS`](#atlas_audit_reads) | `0` | set | no | atlas-api |
| [`ATLAS_AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS`](#atlas_audit_retention_days) | - | set | no | atlas-api |

### `ATLAS_AUDIT_READS`

With ATLAS_AUDIT_READS=1 every agent (service-token) read of a node, a search or a document writes an audit_read row (person, agent, token id, MCP tool, node ids, request id). GET /api/audit/export streams graph_event, auth_event and audit_read as JSON Lines to an owner, or to an owner's agent token minted with `read,admin`.

- **Allowed:** 1 or 0 (also true/false, yes/no, on/off)
- **Default:** `0`
- **OSS install:** `1`, set in `.env.example`
- **Secret:** no
- **Read by:** atlas-api

### `ATLAS_AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS`

Days of audit_read kept. Enforced by `atlas-admin audit purge`, which you schedule, e.g. 0 3 * * * docker compose exec -T atlas-api atlas-admin audit purge Only audit_read is purged; graph_event and auth_event are kept forever.

- **Allowed:** 1 to 36500 days
- **Default:** none (unset)
- **OSS install:** `365`, set in `.env.example`
- **Secret:** no
- **Read by:** atlas-api

### `ATLAS_BACKUP_KEEP`

How many routine backups to keep (1-1000, default 7). After each verified routine backup the older routine backups are deleted; manual, per-deploy and crunch backups are never deleted by it.

### `ATLAS_BACKUP_SCHEDULE`

A routine backup outside crunch week: off (default), hourly, daily or weekly. The crunch policy is still asked first; a routine backup is taken only when the crunch took none.

- **Allowed:** `off`, `hourly`, `daily`, `weekly`
- **Default:** `off`
- **OSS install:** not set; `.env.example` shows `daily` commented out
- **Secret:** no
- **Read by:** atlas-api

### `ATLAS_BACKUP_HOST_DIR`

An absolute host directory for the backup files instead of the `atlas-backups` volume, so they can be copied off this host. Create it first, writable by the container's group 0 (`sudo install -d -m 0770 -g 0 /srv/atlas-backups`).

- **Allowed:** see the description
- **Default:** the compose file's; not read by the Atlas code
- **OSS install:** not set; `.env.example` shows `/srv/atlas-backups` commented out
- **Secret:** no
- **Read by:** docker compose: atlas-backup's backup volume

### `ATLAS_DB_CA_SOURCE`

An external or managed PostgreSQL instead of atlas-postgres: the overlay external-db.yml (docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f external-db.yml, or COMPOSE_FILE=docker-compose.yml:external-db.yml). The URL stays in ./secrets/db_url; docs/oss/guides/external-postgres.md has the steps. The HOST file external-db.yml makes the db_ca secret from: the database server's CA, mounted at /run/secrets/db_ca, which the URL names (?sslmode=verify-full&sslrootcert=/run/secrets/db_ca). Read by the compose file only. Unset: /dev/null, an empty mount nothing reads (sslmode=require).

- **Allowed:** see the description
- **Default:** the compose file's; not read by the Atlas code
- **OSS install:** not set; `.env.example` shows `./secrets/db-ca.crt` commented out
- **Secret:** no
- **Read by:** docker compose: external-db.yml's db_ca secret mounted into atlas-migrate, atlas-api and atlas-backup

### `ATLAS_EMBED_KEY_SOURCE`

The HOST file retrieval.yml makes the embed_key secret from (read by the compose file only). Unset: ./secrets/embed_key. In entra mode set /dev/null, so no key file has to exist.

- **Allowed:** see the description
- **Default:** the compose file's; not read by the Atlas code
- **OSS install:** not set; `.env.example` shows `/dev/null` commented out
- **Secret:** no
- **Read by:** docker compose: retrieval.yml's secret mounted into atlas-api

### `ATLAS_GATEWAY_BIND`

The port and interface of the gateway's TLS door. *(This comment covers `ATLAS_GATEWAY_PORT` too.)*

- **Allowed:** see the description
- **Default:** the compose file's; not read by the Atlas code
- **OSS install:** `0.0.0.0`, set in `.env.example`
- **Secret:** no
- **Read by:** docker compose: atlas-gateway's published port

### `ATLAS_GATEWAY_PORT`

The port and interface of the gateway's TLS door. *(This comment covers `ATLAS_GATEWAY_BIND` too.)*

- **Allowed:** see the description
- **Default:** the compose file's; not read by the Atlas code
- **OSS install:** `8444`, set in `.env.example`
- **Secret:** no
- **Read by:** docker compose: atlas-gateway's published port

### `ATLAS_GATEWAY_SESSION_KEY_FILE`

MCP session-ID encryption through the gateway (TASK-1460): off unless this names a key file. Off, the gateway's MCP session IDs are only base64-encoded (a session ID is a routing handle, not a credential: every call still carries its own token). On, they are AES-256-GCM encrypted with a 32-byte key, kept in a file you create, 0600 and owned by you: `( umask 077; openssl rand -hex 32 &gt; ./secrets/gateway_session_key )` render-gateway.py reads this setting (not docker compose): it reads the key from the file (a path relative to this directory, or absolute) and writes it into ./gateway/agentgateway.yaml, which it then writes 0600 (AgentGateway v1.7.0 takes the key only inline in its config or as an environment variable). The key itself never goes in this file. Render again and recreate atlas-gateway after setting, changing or unsetting it; a new key ends every open session.

- **Allowed:** see the description
- **Default:** the compose file's; not read by the Atlas code
- **OSS install:** not set; `.env.example` shows `./secrets/gateway_session_key` commented out
- **Secret:** yes: this is the path of a file holding a credential
- **Read by:** scripts/render-gateway.py (not docker compose): the key render-gateway.py writes into ./gateway/agentgateway.yaml as config.session.key (that file then 0600)

- **Read by:** docker compose: atlas-tls's site name (CADDY_PUBLIC_HOST); atlas-api's healthcheck sends it as Host

### `ATLAS_TLS_BIND`

The port the TLS ingress is published on, and the interface. 443 on every interface by default: this is the install's one door and it is HTTPS. Use 127.0.0.1 to keep it local. *(This comment covers `ATLAS_TLS_PORT` too.)*

- **Allowed:** see the description
- **Default:** the compose file's; not read by the Atlas code
- **OSS install:** `0.0.0.0`, set in `.env.example`
- **Secret:** no
- **Read by:** docker compose: atlas-tls's published port

### `ATLAS_TLS_CF_TOKEN_FILE`

acme-cloudflare only: the PATH of a file holding the token, never the token.

- **Allowed:** see the description
- **Default:** the compose file's; not read by the Atlas code
- **OSS install:** not set; `.env.example` shows `./secrets/cf_dns_api_token` commented out
- **Secret:** yes: this is the path of a file holding a credential
- **Read by:** docker compose: the cf_dns_api_token secret mounted into atlas-tls

### `ATLAS_TLS_CLIENT_AUTH`

The mTLS leg on atlas-mcp's hop to the API: off (default) \| require. With require, atlas-tls refuses a connection to atlas-api:9443 without a client certificate issued by the CA in ATLAS_TLS_CLIENT_CA_FILE (default ./secrets/tls/client-ca.crt), and atlas-mcp presents its own: uncomment the two ATLAS_MCP_CLIENT_* lines together with this one. *(This comment covers `ATLAS_TLS_CLIENT_CA_FILE`, `ATLAS_MCP_CLIENT_CERT_FILE`, `ATLAS_MCP_CLIENT_KEY_FILE` too.)*

- **Allowed:** see the description
- **Default:** the compose file's; not read by the Atlas code
- **OSS install:** `off`, set in `.env.example`
- **Secret:** no
- **Read by:** docker compose: atlas-tls (CADDY_CLIENT_AUTH)

### `ATLAS_TLS_CLIENT_CA_FILE`

The mTLS leg on atlas-mcp's hop to the API: off (default) \| require. With require, atlas-tls refuses a connection to atlas-api:9443 without a client certificate issued by the CA in ATLAS_TLS_CLIENT_CA_FILE (default ./secrets/tls/client-ca.crt), and atlas-mcp presents its own: uncomment the two ATLAS_MCP_CLIENT_* lines together with this one. *(This comment covers `ATLAS_TLS_CLIENT_AUTH`, `ATLAS_MCP_CLIENT_CERT_FILE`, `ATLAS_MCP_CLIENT_KEY_FILE` too.)*

- **Allowed:** see the description
- **Default:** the compose file's; not read by the Atlas code
- **OSS install:** not set; `.env.example` shows `./secrets/tls/client-ca.crt` commented out
- **Secret:** no
- **Read by:** docker compose: the client_ca secret mounted into atlas-tls

### `ATLAS_TLS_MODE`

Where the public certificate comes from: files ./secrets/tls/server.crt + server.key (default). init-secrets.sh makes them with init-certs.sh from a throwaway install CA when there is no PKI; with your enterprise PKI, put its files there instead BEFORE running it: ./secrets/tls/server.crt full chain, SANs: ATLAS_PUBLIC_HOST and atlas-api ./secrets/tls/server.key its key ./secrets/tls/ca.crt your root (atlas-mcp trusts exactly this file) internal Caddy's own CA for the public door (clients trust its root, in the atlas-tls-data volume at /data/caddy/pki/authorities/local/root.crt) acme-cloudflare Let's Encrypt by DNS-01; the Cloudflare token in the file named below atlas-mcp's own hop (https://atlas-api:9443) always uses ./secrets/tls/server.crt, checked against ./secrets/tls/ca.crt.

- **Allowed:** see the description
- **Default:** the compose file's; not read by the Atlas code
- **OSS install:** `files`, set in `.env.example`
- **Secret:** no
- **Read by:** docker compose: atlas-tls (CADDY_TLS_MODE)

### `ATLAS_TLS_PORT`

The port the TLS ingress is published on, and the interface. 443 on every interface by default: this is the install's one door and it is HTTPS. Use 127.0.0.1 to keep it local. *(This comment covers `ATLAS_TLS_BIND` too.)*

- **Allowed:** see the description
- **Default:** the compose file's; not read by the Atlas code
- **OSS install:** `443`, set in `.env.example`
- **Secret:** no
- **Read by:** docker compose: atlas-tls's published port
